title: FlashGNN: An In-SSD Accelerator for GNN Training
problem: Single-machine GNN training is bottlenecked by slow PCIe data transfer and flash memory access latency, resulting in low CPU and GPU utilization.
motivation: Real-world graph datasets exceed centralized system capabilities, and distributed systems suffer from network bandwidth limitations.
method: FlashGNN employs a node-wise training approach (processing the graph one node at a time) with coordinating logic built into the SSD firmware. The firmware orchestrates data retrieval to exploit flash memory's ability to read multiple chunks in parallel—simultaneously instead of sequentially—while maximizing data reuse: frequently-needed data stays on the fast flash storage rather than being repeatedly shuttled across the slow PCIe cable. A specialized algorithm schedules which data requests to handle first, and subgraphs are generated to align with the physical layout of data on flash chips.
key_novelty: It places the accelerator inside the SSD's firmware to exploit flash memory's parallel reading capability and bypass the slow PCIe bottleneck.
contributions: In-SSD accelerator design with firmware coordination for data movements and hardware access
Node-wise GNN training method optimized for flash memory access patterns
Efficient flash request scheduling algorithm for I/O parallelism utilization
High-performance subgraph generation method for flash-based GNN processing
